# Adjudication Task — Chapter 179

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃179화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|진짜 원단이네.
  6|
  7|태원진가에서 출발하기 전, 위팽으로부터 신신당부를 들었던 것이 고작 이틀 전인데 까맣게 잊고 있었다.
  8|
  9|헛숨을 삼킨 혁무진이 말했다.
 10|
 11|“어, 어떡하죠?”
 12|
 13|“어떡하긴 뭘 어떡해. 어차피 알고 있었어도 제시간에 못 맞췄을 텐데.”
 14|
 15|다른 사람도 아니고 무려 화왕이다. 어제 분위기를 감안해 봤을 때, 집안일이 있어 이만 가 보겠다고 했으면 호쾌하게 보내 줬을 거다.
 16|
 17|물론 집이 아니라 황천길로.
 18|
 19|“위 대협께서 절 죽이실 겁니다.”
 20|
 21|나는 안색이 거무죽죽해진 혁무진의 어깨를 두드려 주었다.
 22|
 23|“괜찮아. 난 못 죽일걸.”
 24|
 25|“오, 저도요!”
 26|
 27|“…….”
 28|
 29|이게 바로 뒷배 없는 자의 서러움이지.
 30|
 31|하지만 굳이 늑장 부릴 생각은 없다.
 32|
 33|명색이 태원진가가 산서성의 지배자로 우뚝 서는 날인데 그 집안 막내가 늦어서야 쓰나.
 34|
 35|“짐 챙겨. 바로 출발한다.”
 36|
 37|짐이라고 해 봤자 행낭 하나가 전부지만.
 38|
 39|순식간에 준비를 끝마친 우리는 1층으로 내려갔다. 원단을 맞아 온통 붉게 장식된 객잔 안은 이른 아침임에도 불구하고 사람들로 북적거렸다.
 40|
 41|그리고 그들 중, 유난히 눈에 띄는 두 사람이 있었다.
 42|
 43|“오, 지금 일어났나?”
 44|
 45|“쯧쯧. 젊은 놈들이 저렇게 잠이 많아서야.”
 46|
 47|“그러게 말입니다. 저 젊을 적에는 하루 한 시진도 못 자는 날이 허다했는데.”
 48|
 49|“한 시진이나? 이보게, 나 때는 말이야…….”
 50|
 51|손을 들어 알은척하더니 이내 자기들끼리 술잔을 주고받는 두 노인.
 52|
 53|벌겋게 달아오른 얼굴과 옆에 놓인 술동이는 낮부터 거하게 한 잔 걸쳤다는 증거다.
 54|
 55|뒤따라 내려오던 혁무진이 작은 목소리로 속삭였다.
 56|
 57|“저게 무슨 조합입니까?”
 58|
 59|“나도 몰라.”
 60|
 61|한 명은 어지간한 장정보다 몸집이 큰 거구의 노인이고, 다른 한 명은 입김을 불면 날아갈 것 같은 왜소한 체격이다.
 62|
 63|화왕이야 그렇다치고.
 64|
 65|‘장태보, 저 양반은 언제 왔대?’
 66|
 67|의뢰 때문에 온 건가?
 68|
 69|어쨌건 각자의 분야에서 일가(一家)를 이룬 두 노인은 어느샌가 꽤 친해진 듯 보였다.
 70|
 71|“분위기 어수선한데 그냥 슬쩍 나가면 안 됩니까?”
 72|
 73|“슬쩍 같은 소리 하네. 너 어제 오리 뼈로 얻어맞고 기절한 거 기억 안 나냐?”
 74|
 75|“그게 오리 뼈였어요? 젠장, 어쩐지 골이 울리더라.”
 76|
 77|“모른 척하고 나갔다가는 골이 빠개질걸.”
 78|
 79|“그건 좀.”
 80|
 81|“어때, 도망칠래?”
 82|
 83|혁무진이 침울한 얼굴로 한숨을 내쉬었다.
 84|
 85|“후우, 새해 첫날부터 재수 옴 붙었네.”
 86|
 87|백번 공감한다. 새해 첫날 아침부터 화왕 적천강을 만나고 싶은 사람은 어디에도 없을 테니까.
 88|
 89|“할아버지들, 만두 없어요?”
 90|
 91|“고기도 많이 있다. 먹어라.”
 92|
 93|“와아!”
 94|
 95|……저놈 빼고.
 96|
 97|나와 혁무진은 도살장에 끌려가는 소처럼 무거운 마음으로 걸음을 옮겼다.
 98|
 99|빛의 속도로 음식들을 쑤셔 넣고 있던 청풍이 해맑게 웃으며 접시들을 내밀었다.
100|
101|“으이! 마이어으! 드스 브스으!”
102|
103|“……너나 많이 드세요.”
104|
105|“즈 므그스느드!”
106|
107|이런 녀석이 절정 고수라니. 이 불공평한 현실에 통탄을 금하지 못하겠다.
108|
109|무림의 앞날을 걱정하던 내게 장태보가 말을 건넸다.
110|
111|“그래, 자네들은 이제 어찌할 셈인가?”
112|
113|“우선 본가로 돌아갈 생각입니다. 일이 좀 있어서요.”
114|
115|“아, 그렇군. 태원진가에서 회합이 있다고 했나?”
116|
117|현재 산서성 내에서 태원진가에 관한 일거수일투족은 뜨거운 감자다.
118|
119|늙은 호랑이 취급받던 태원진가가 오랜 세월 끝에 산서 무림이라는 옥좌(玉座)에 다시 앉게 되었으니, 그 관심과 기대가 보통이 아닐 만도 했다.
120|
121|장가촌 같은 조그마한 마을에서 집돌이 생활을 하는 장태보마저 알고 있을 정도니까.
122|
123|“근래에 사람들이 모이기만 하면 그 얘기더군. 무림과는 하등 관련도 없는 양민들까지 눈요기한다고 몰려갈 정도니 말 다 했지.”
124|
125|“설마 그렇게까지 올까요.”
126|
127|“진수성찬에는 온갖 잡다한 것들이 끼어드는 법이지. 산서성이 제아무리 변방에 속한다지만 일성의 패주(霸主)가 되는 자리일세. 내 비록 무림인은 아니지만 보고 들은 경륜은 제법 되니 기대해 보게. 아, 그리고…….”
128|
129|장태보가 낮은 목소리로 한마디를 덧붙였다.
130|
131|“의뢰에 관해서는 걱정일랑 하지 말고.”
132|
133|의뢰. 그 말을 듣자 문득 생각나는 것이 있었다.
134|
135|당시에는 겨를이 없어 미처 묻지 못한 말이다.
136|
137|“저기, 혹시 따로 필요하거나 그런 건 없으세요?”
138|
139|“뭘 말인가?”
140|
141|“여러 가지가 있지 않겠습니까.”
142|
143|동네 세탁소에 가도 수선비를 주는데, 장태보는 천하에서 이름 높은 장인이다. 비록 현역 때만큼은 아니겠지만 그 실력이 십 년 동안 증발했다고는 생각하지 않는다.
144|
145|그럼 분명 그만한 대가가 있어야 할 텐데…….
146|
147|내 말뜻을 알아차린 장태보가 흰 수염을 쓸었다.
148|
149|“사례를 하겠다. 뭐 그런 건가?”
150|
151|“솔직히 말씀드려서 기대하시는 것만큼은 못 해 드립니다.”
152|
153|“그럼 만 냥만 주게.”
154|
155|만 냥이면 은자 백 냥이다. 분명 엄청난 거금이지만 그의 명성을 감안하면 특가 할인이나 다름없게 느껴졌다.
156|
157|나는 시원하게 고개를 끄덕였다. 어차피 내 돈도 아닌데 뭐.
158|
159|“준비해서 자택으로 보내 드리겠습니다.”
160|
161|“은자 만 냥을? 태원 진가 기둥뿌리를 죄다 뽑아야겠구먼.”
162|
163|“……은자로 만 냥이요?”
164|
165|“당연하지. 내 몸값이 그렇게 싸구려로 보였나?”
166|
167|“그럼 자그마치 백만 냥인데.”
168|
169|“자그마치가 아니라 겨우 백만 냥이지. 천하제일의 신병이기를 얻을 수 있는데 그깟 재물이 대수인가?”
170|
171|“…….”
172|
173|당연히 대수지.
174|
175|백만 냥이면 현실에서 얼마야, 수천억? 아니면 조 단위?
176|
177|내 표정을 본 장태보가 피식 웃으며 입을 열었다.
178|
179|“필요 없네.”
180|
181|“죄송하지만 혹시 만 냥으로 쿨거래 가능하십니…… 예?”
182|
183|“필요 없다고. 내가 그거 받아서 뭐 하겠나? 죽을 때까지 다 쓰지도 못할 텐데. 살아생전 이런 기회가 온 것만으로도 충분해.”
184|
185|이런 것이 바로 장인 정신인가?
186|
187|그야말로 빛태보. 천하의 야장들은 그를 본받아 태보해야 한다.
188|
189|내가 감동으로 몸을 부르르 떨고 있던 그때 혁무진이 존경스럽다는 표정으로 끼어들었다.
190|
191|“그럼 일단 만 냥만 받으시고 그거 저 주시면 안 됩니까?”
192|
193|저 새끼는 자서전 써도 될 것 같다. 제목은 [맞아 뒤지는 방법 100선].
194|
195|놈의 뒤통수를 후려친 나는 장태보에게 공손히 고개를 숙였다.
196|
197|“그럼 모쪼록 부탁드립니다.”
198|
199|“부탁은 내가 해야지. 기간이 얼마나 걸릴지는 장담하기 힘들지만, 분명 세상을 떨어 울릴 만한 물건이 나올 걸세. 그러니 부디 그때까지 그에 걸맞은 힘과 자격을 갖춰 주게.”
200|
201|“노력하겠습니다.”
202|
203|“그래, 그럼 된 거지. 자네를 믿어 보는 수밖에.”
204|
205|고개를 끄덕이던 장태보가 멈칫했다.
206|
207|“아. 그리고 하나만 부탁해도 되겠나?”
208|
209|“……?”
210|
211|“집 좀 다시 지어 주게. 죄다 불에 타서 잠잘 곳도 없어.”
212|
213|은퇴 후 장만한 집. 편안한 노후를 보내던 소중한 공간이 하루아침에 사라졌다.
214|
215|장태보의 서글픈 목소리에 시선이 저절로 옆을 향했다. 우리가 대화를 나누는 동안 조용히 술잔을 꺾고 있던 적천강이 눈을 치켜뜬다.
216|
217|“뭘 봐.”
218|
219|지난밤의 감성적이고 진지하던 적천강의 모습은 찾아볼 수 없다. 나는 슬쩍 시선을 회피했다.
220|
221|“……아무것도 아닙니다.”
222|
223|“할 말 있으면 해라. 노부는 그리 속 좁은 사람이 아니다.”
224|
225|“진짜 해도 됩니까?”
226|
227|“해 봐.”
228|
229|말이 끝남과 동시에 탁자 아래가 뜨겁게 달아오른다.
230|
231|알고 보니 객잔 주인이 현대인이라 전기난로를 가져다 뒀을 리는 없고…….
232|
233|‘시발, 화염신장.’
234|
235|나는 눈물을 머금고 대답했다.
236|
237|“그냥, 오늘따라 십 년은 젊어 보이신다는 생각을 하고 있었습니다.”
238|
239|적천강이 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
240|
241|“뭐라, 십 년?”
242|
243|젠장, 생각해 보니 백 살에서 십 년 빼 봤자 구십이네.
244|
245|나는 재빨리 말을 바꿨다.
246|
247|“이십 년…….”
248|
249|“이십 년?”
250|
251|“삼십 년…….”
252|
253|불과 3초 남짓한 시간 만에 삼십 년이나 회춘한 적천강이 흐뭇하게 고개를 끄덕였다.
254|
255|“머리에 똥만 찬 놈인 줄 알았는데, 네 녀석도 제법 그럴듯한 생각을 하는구나.”
256|
257|“…….”
258|
259|혁무진은 할 말이 있는 표정이었지만 입을 꾹 다물었다.
260|
261|아무래도 [맞아 뒤지는 방법 100선]을 유작으로 만들고 싶은 생각은 없는 모양이다.
262|
263|대신 내 옆구리를 쿡쿡 찌르는 것이, 당장이라도 이 자리를 뜨고 싶은 마음이 간절해 보였다.
264|
265|‘물론 그건 나도 마찬가지고.’
266|
267|그러기 위해서는 마무리 지어야 할 일이 하나 있지.
268|
269|나는 최대한 공손한 어투로 입을 열었다.
270|
271|“제가 맡고 있는 물건이 몇 개 있습니다.”
272|
273|불콰한 얼굴로 술잔을 기울이던 적천강이 피식 웃었다.
274|
275|“돌려줄 생각은 있었고?”
276|
277|“당연히 돌려드려야죠.”
278|
279|“그렇지. 안 돌려주면 험한 꼴을 보게 될 테니.”
280|
281|“…….”
282|
283|노인네, 사람 속 귀신같이 꿰뚫어 보는 것 보소.
284|
285|나는 억지웃음을 지으며 미리 꺼내 놓은 물건들을 탁자에 올렸다. 조필에게서 얻은 [화염신장]의 비급. 그리고 만년한철로 만들어진 [이름 없는 검]이다.
286|
287|“적 대협께서도 이미 알고 계시겠지만 열화신단은…….”
288|
289|“네놈이 처먹었지.”
290|
291|“예. 그렇죠.”
292|
293|“한데…….”
294|
295|주름진 손가락이 탁자를 두드린다. 적천강의 마른 목소리가 이어졌다.
296|
297|“보옥(寶玉)은 어디 있느냐?”
298|
299|“예?”
300|
301|“보옥 말이다. 보옥.”
302|
303|보옥이라면 보물, 보석. 뭐 그런 거?
304|
305|적천강이 일반적인 보석류 따위에 집착할 성격은 아니니 매우 중요한 물건임에는 확실해 보인다.
306|
307|그러나 보옥의 존재를 모르고 있던 나로서는 황당할 뿐이었다.
308|
309|“제가 받은 건 이게 전부인데요.”
310|
311|“받아? 네가 직접 거둔 것이 아니란 말이냐?”
312|
313|“네. 사정이 있어서 깨어난 직후에 건네받았습니다.”
314|
315|“그중 의심이 가는 놈은 없고?”
316|
317|조필의 물건을 전해 준 것은 공야청과 소천이다. 그리고 두 사람 다 뭔가를 뒤로 슬쩍 빼돌릴 만한 이들이 아니다.
318|
319|그 자리에 있던 정찰조원들도 마찬가지다. 어떻게 된 일인지는 모르지만 그들을 믿는 마음은 변함이 없다.
320|
321|“아닐 겁니다. 아니, 절대 아닙니다.”
322|

“Thanksh, I will!”

[P53]
Someone like him was a Peak master. The sheer unfairness of reality filled me with despair for the future of the Murim.

[P54]
Jang Taebo spoke up.

[P55]
“So, what are you all planning to do now?”

[P56]
“We’re going back to our family first. We have some business to take care of.”

[P57]
“Ah, I see. You said there was going to be a gathering at the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”

[P58]
At present, every move the Jin Family of Taiyuan made was a hot topic throughout Shanxi Province.

[P59]
After many long years, the Jin Family of Taiyuan—once dismissed as an old tiger past its prime—had reclaimed the throne of the Shanxi Murim. No wonder expectations were running so high.

[P60]
Even Jang Taebo, a homebody living in a tiny place like Jang Family Village, had heard about it.

[P61]
“That’s all anyone talks about whenever people gather these days. Even ordinary people with nothing to do with the Murim are flocking there for the spectacle. That tells you everything.”

[P62]
“Will that many people really come?”

[P63]
“A grand feast always draws all sorts of hangers-on. Shanxi Province may be a frontier region, but this is about becoming the hegemon of an entire province. I may not be a martial artist, but I’ve seen and heard enough in my time. Just wait and see. Ah, and…”

[P64]
Jang Taebo lowered his voice.

[P65]
“Don’t worry about the commission.”

[P66]
The commission.

[P67]
His words suddenly reminded me of something I hadn’t had the chance to ask before.

[P68]
“By the way, is there anything else you need?”

[P69]
“What do you mean?”

[P70]
“Well, there must be something.”

[P71]
Even the neighborhood laundromat charged for repairs. Jang Taebo was a master artisan renowned throughout the world. He might not be as skilled as he had been in his prime, but there was no way ten years had made all that ability vanish.

[P72]
His work had to command an appropriate price…

[P73]
Realizing what I meant, Jang Taebo stroked his white beard.

[P74]
“You mean you want to compensate me?”

[P75]
“To be honest, I probably can’t give you as much as you’re expecting.”

[P76]
“Then just give me ten thousand nyang.”

[P77]
Ten thousand nyang was a hundred silver nyang. It was certainly an enormous sum, but considering his reputation, it felt like a bargain.

[P78]
I nodded readily. It wasn’t my money, anyway.

[P79]
“I’ll prepare it and send it to your home.”

[P80]
“Ten thousand silver nyang? You’d have to tear out every last pillar holding up the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P81]
“…Ten thousand *silver* nyang?”

[P82]
“Of course. Did you think my services were that cheap?”

[P83]
“That’s a whopping million nyang.”

[P84]
“Not a whopping million. A mere million. You’ll be getting the greatest divine weapon under heaven. What does a little money matter?”

[P85]
“…”

[P86]
Of course it mattered.

[P87]
How much would a million nyang be worth in the real world? Hundreds of billions of won? Trillions?

[P88]
Jang Taebo let out a quiet laugh at my expression.

[P89]
“I don’t need it.”

[P90]
“I’m sorry, but would you consider a quick deal for ten thousand nyang—pardon?”

[P91]
“I said I don’t need it. What would I do with that much money? I couldn’t spend it all before I died. Having an opportunity like this come my way while I’m still alive is payment enough.”

[P92]
Was this the spirit of a true artisan?

[P93]
Glorious Taebo. Every blacksmith under heaven should follow his example—and take up Tae Bo.

[P94]
As I trembled with emotion, Hyuk Mujin cut in with an admiring look.

[P95]
“Then could you take the ten thousand nyang and give it to me?”

[P96]
That bastard could write an autobiography. He could call it *A Hundred Ways to Get Yourself Beaten to Death*.

[P97]
I smacked him on the back of the head, then bowed politely to Jang Taebo.

[P98]
“Then I’ll leave it in your hands.”

[P99]
“I’m the one who should be asking a favor. I can’t promise how long it will take, but I’ll create something that will make the world tremble. Until then, make sure you acquire the strength and qualifications worthy of wielding it.”

[P100]
“I’ll do my best.”

[P101]
“Good. Then that settles it. I’ll have to place my trust in you.”

[P102]
Jang Taebo nodded, then paused.

[P103]
“Ah. Could I ask one more favor?”

[P104]
“…?”

[P105]
“Build me another house. The old one burned to the ground, and now I don’t even have anywhere to sleep.”

[P106]
The home he had bought after retiring—the precious place where he had spent his golden years in peace—had vanished overnight.

[P107]
At the sorrow in Jang Taebo’s voice, my gaze drifted to the side of its own accord.

[P108]
Jeok Cheongang, who had been quietly sipping his wine while we talked, looked up.

[P109]
“What are you staring at?”

[P110]
There was no trace of the emotional, solemn Jeok Cheongang from last night. I subtly averted my gaze.

[P111]
“…Nothing.”

[P112]
“If you have something to say, say it. This old man isn’t so petty.”

[P113]
“Are you sure?”

[P114]
“Go ahead.”

[P115]
The moment he finished speaking, the air beneath the table began to heat up.

[P116]
It wasn’t as though the innkeeper was a modern man who had installed an electric heater…

[P117]
*Fuck. Flame Divine Palm.*

[P118]
Tears welled in my eyes as I answered.

[P119]
“I was just thinking that you looked a good ten years younger today.”

[P120]
Jeok Cheongang frowned.

[P121]
“What? Ten years?”

[P122]
Damn it. Subtracting ten from a hundred still left ninety.

[P123]
I hurriedly revised my answer.

[P124]
“Twenty years…”

[P125]
“Twenty years?”

[P126]
“Thirty years…”

[P127]
In the space of barely three seconds, Jeok Cheongang had grown thirty years younger. He nodded in satisfaction.

[P128]
“I thought your head was filled with nothing but shit, but it seems even you have a sensible thought now and then.”

[P129]
“…”

[P130]
Hyuk Mujin looked like he had something to say, but he clamped his mouth shut.

[P131]
Apparently, he had no desire to make *A Hundred Ways to Get Yourself Beaten to Death* his final work.

[P132]
Instead, he kept poking me in the side, plainly desperate to leave.

[P133]
*Of course, I feel the same way.*

[P134]
But before we could go, there was one last thing I needed to settle.

[P135]
I spoke in the most respectful tone I could manage.

[P136]
“I have a few items in my possession.”

[P137]
Jeok Cheongang, his face flushed as he tipped back his wine cup, let out a quiet laugh.

[P138]
“Were you ever planning to return them?”

[P139]
“Of course.”

[P140]
“You should. If you don’t, things will get ugly.”

[P141]
“…”

[P142]
The old man could see right through me.

[P143]
I forced a smile and placed the items I had prepared on the table.

[P144]
The Flame Divine Palm martial arts manual I had obtained from Jopil, and the Unnamed Sword made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.

[P145]
“As you already know, Great Hero Jeok, the Blazing Flame Divine Pill…”

[P146]
“You gobbled it up.”

[P147]
“Yes. That’s right.”

[P148]
“But…”

[P149]
A wrinkled finger tapped against the table. Jeok Cheongang continued in a dry voice.

[P150]
“Where is the Treasured Jade?”

[P151]
“Pardon?”

[P152]
“The Treasured Jade. Where is it?”

[P153]
Treasured jade? As in some sort of treasure or gemstone?

[P154]
Jeok Cheongang didn’t seem like the type to obsess over ordinary jewelry, so it had to be extremely important.

[P155]
But since I hadn’t even known it existed, I could only stare at him in bewilderment.

[P156]
“These are the only things I received.”

[P157]
“Received? You didn’t collect them yourself?”

[P158]
“No. There were circumstances. They were handed to me right after I woke up.”

[P159]
“Do you suspect any of the people involved?”

[P160]
Gong Yacheong and Socheon had handed Jopil’s belongings over to me. Neither of them was the sort to quietly pocket something behind everyone else’s back.

[P161]
The same went for the members of the reconnaissance squad who had been there. I didn’t know what had happened, but that didn’t change my trust in them.

[P162]
“They wouldn’t have. No, absolutely not.”

[P163]
Jeok Cheongang studied me for a moment before speaking.

[P164]
“Then it must be one of two things. Someone deceived you, or that child lost it.”

[P165]
“…”

[P166]
“What a nuisance. This has become troublesome.”

[P167]
Jeok Cheongang had likely returned to the world not only to find his Disciple, but also to recover the Fire Gate Clan’s treasures that had been scattered because of him.

[P168]
The Treasured Jade seemed to be one of them.

[P169]
A treasure so important that even the Fire King was willing to go through the trouble of searching for it.

[P170]
*Damn it. I never even got to see it.*

[P171]
A creeping sense of danger began to overwhelm my curiosity about what the Treasured Jade actually was.

[P172]
“It can’t be helped. Keep them for now.”

[P173]
That casual remark brought my thoughts to a complete halt.

[P174]
Wait. Did he mean…

[P175]
“You want me to keep these?”

[P176]
“Yes.”

[P177]
“Both of them?”

[P178]
“All three. Have you forgotten the one in your stomach? Anything that originated from our sect must be reclaimed, one way or another.”

[P179]
“…!”

[P180]
“I’m joking.”

[P181]
“Phew.”

[P182]
“Tsk, tsk. You’re still young, but your nerve is already the size of a bean.”

[P183]
Bean or cannonball, I didn’t care.

[P184]
I wanted nothing more to do with that terrifying old man. Ever.

[P185]
I took a deep breath.

[P186]
“I’m sorry, but I’ll have to decline—”

[P187]
“If you refuse, I’ll reclaim them right now. All three.”

[P188]
“…”

[P189]
“This time, I’m serious.”

[P190]
Once again, the air beneath the table grew scorching hot. There was no need to guess which technique it was.

[P191]
*What the fuck?*

[P192]
I was trying to return everything to its rightful owner, and I wasn’t even allowed to do that?

[P193]
Overcome with resentment and indignation, I demanded, “Why are you doing this to me?”

[P194]
“Do you expect an old man like me to carry around all that cumbersome junk? I don’t have the strength.”

[P195]
“What if someone takes them from me?”

[P196]
“Then this old man will kill you.”

[P197]
“What if I learn the martial art?”

[P198]
“Then you’ll die even more painfully.”

[P199]
What kind of bullshit situation was this?

[P200]
Leaving me standing there in a daze, the Fire King rose from his seat.

[P201]
Cheongpung, who was still cramming food into his mouth, looked up.

[P202]
“Gwandpa, awe you leaving?”

[P203]
“…You’re even worse than your grandfather. Slow down.”

[P204]
After exchanging a farewell glance with Jang Taebo, Jeok Cheongang turned away and tossed out an ominous remark.

[P205]
“Let’s meet again soon.”

[P206]
I didn’t want to see him.

[P207]
Ever.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 179

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃179화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|진짜 원단이네.
  6|
  7|태원진가에서 출발하기 전, 위팽으로부터 신신당부를 들었던 것이 고작 이틀 전인데 까맣게 잊고 있었다.
  8|
  9|헛숨을 삼킨 혁무진이 말했다.
 10|
 11|“어, 어떡하죠?”
 12|
 13|“어떡하긴 뭘 어떡해. 어차피 알고 있었어도 제시간에 못 맞췄을 텐데.”
 14|
 15|다른 사람도 아니고 무려 화왕이다. 어제 분위기를 감안해 봤을 때, 집안일이 있어 이만 가 보겠다고 했으면 호쾌하게 보내 줬을 거다.
 16|
 17|물론 집이 아니라 황천길로.
 18|
 19|“위 대협께서 절 죽이실 겁니다.”
 20|
 21|나는 안색이 거무죽죽해진 혁무진의 어깨를 두드려 주었다.
 22|
 23|“괜찮아. 난 못 죽일걸.”
 24|
 25|“오, 저도요!”
 26|
 27|“…….”
 28|
 29|이게 바로 뒷배 없는 자의 서러움이지.
 30|
 31|하지만 굳이 늑장 부릴 생각은 없다.
 32|
 33|명색이 태원진가가 산서성의 지배자로 우뚝 서는 날인데 그 집안 막내가 늦어서야 쓰나.
 34|
 35|“짐 챙겨. 바로 출발한다.”
 36|
 37|짐이라고 해 봤자 행낭 하나가 전부지만.
 38|
 39|순식간에 준비를 끝마친 우리는 1층으로 내려갔다. 원단을 맞아 온통 붉게 장식된 객잔 안은 이른 아침임에도 불구하고 사람들로 북적거렸다.
 40|
 41|그리고 그들 중, 유난히 눈에 띄는 두 사람이 있었다.
 42|
 43|“오, 지금 일어났나?”
 44|
 45|“쯧쯧. 젊은 놈들이 저렇게 잠이 많아서야.”
 46|
 47|“그러게 말입니다. 저 젊을 적에는 하루 한 시진도 못 자는 날이 허다했는데.”
 48|
 49|“한 시진이나? 이보게, 나 때는 말이야…….”
 50|
 51|손을 들어 알은척하더니 이내 자기들끼리 술잔을 주고받는 두 노인.
 52|
 53|벌겋게 달아오른 얼굴과 옆에 놓인 술동이는 낮부터 거하게 한 잔 걸쳤다는 증거다.
 54|
 55|뒤따라 내려오던 혁무진이 작은 목소리로 속삭였다.
 56|
 57|“저게 무슨 조합입니까?”
 58|
 59|“나도 몰라.”
 60|
 61|한 명은 어지간한 장정보다 몸집이 큰 거구의 노인이고, 다른 한 명은 입김을 불면 날아갈 것 같은 왜소한 체격이다.
 62|
 63|화왕이야 그렇다치고.
 64|
 65|‘장태보, 저 양반은 언제 왔대?’
 66|
 67|의뢰 때문에 온 건가?
 68|
 69|어쨌건 각자의 분야에서 일가(一家)를 이룬 두 노인은 어느샌가 꽤 친해진 듯 보였다.
 70|
 71|“분위기 어수선한데 그냥 슬쩍 나가면 안 됩니까?”
 72|
 73|“슬쩍 같은 소리 하네. 너 어제 오리 뼈로 얻어맞고 기절한 거 기억 안 나냐?”
 74|
 75|“그게 오리 뼈였어요? 젠장, 어쩐지 골이 울리더라.”
 76|
 77|“모른 척하고 나갔다가는 골이 빠개질걸.”
 78|
 79|“그건 좀.”
 80|
 81|“어때, 도망칠래?”
 82|
 83|혁무진이 침울한 얼굴로 한숨을 내쉬었다.
 84|
 85|“후우, 새해 첫날부터 재수 옴 붙었네.”
 86|
 87|백번 공감한다. 새해 첫날 아침부터 화왕 적천강을 만나고 싶은 사람은 어디에도 없을 테니까.
 88|
 89|“할아버지들, 만두 없어요?”
 90|
 91|“고기도 많이 있다. 먹어라.”
 92|
 93|“와아!”
 94|
 95|……저놈 빼고.
 96|
 97|나와 혁무진은 도살장에 끌려가는 소처럼 무거운 마음으로 걸음을 옮겼다.
 98|
 99|빛의 속도로 음식들을 쑤셔 넣고 있던 청풍이 해맑게 웃으며 접시들을 내밀었다.
100|
101|“으이! 마이어으! 드스 브스으!”
102|
103|“……너나 많이 드세요.”
104|
105|“즈 므그스느드!”
106|
107|이런 녀석이 절정 고수라니. 이 불공평한 현실에 통탄을 금하지 못하겠다.
108|
109|무림의 앞날을 걱정하던 내게 장태보가 말을 건넸다.
110|
111|“그래, 자네들은 이제 어찌할 셈인가?”
112|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
